findings.issue_text: [BUG] The dataclass default `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once at module import time, and the resulting datetime value is then shipped through `to_dict()` into Celery `apply_async` kwargs, where the default JSON serializer raises EncodeError because datetime is not JSON-serializable. The first cross-integration inbound assign (assignment_source non-None) calls sync_group_assignee_outbound.apply_async with a kwargs payload containing a raw datetime; with the default Celery JSON serializer the task fails to enqueue (EncodeError), so the assignee never propagates to the other linked integration, silently breaking the feature this PR exists to deliver. Additionally, every AssignmentSource created after process start reports a `queued` timestamp equal to import time, so the field's value is wrong.

[BUG] The task now calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(external_issue, user, assign=assign, assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source)`, but the concrete `sync_assignee_outbound` implementations of existing integrations (Jira, GitHub, GitLab, etc., not touched by this diff) define signatures like `(self, external_issue, user, assign=True)` without `assignment_source`, so passing the new keyword raises TypeError. Whenever an assignment flows inbound from one integration and a second, different integration is also linked to the group (the exact multi-integration propagation scenario the diff claims to support), should_sync returns True for the second integration, the task invokes its sync_assignee_outbound with the unexpected `assignment_source` kwarg, and the task crashes with TypeError — the assignee change is never propagated and the sync fails loudly in task processing.

[ADVISORY] `from_dict` returns None for any malformed payload, which the task layer then treats identically to 'no source' (sync proceeds), so a payload that fails to round-trip through the queue silently disables cycle-prevention rather than failing. If a broker/serializer mutates or strips the dict (e.g., an old worker during a rolling deploy that doesn't know the kwarg, or a serialization edge on `queued`), from_dict swallows the damage and returns None, causing the same-integration sync cycle the design was built to prevent — a loop of assign/unassign between Sentry and the external issue with no error surfaced.

[BUG] The frozen dataclass field `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` evaluates `timezone.now()` once at class-definition (module import) time, so every AssignmentSource instance shares the process-start timestamp instead of the enqueue time. All assignment_source records carry a stale import-time `queued` value; any consumer relying on it for cycle-window/dedup logic or latency measurement gets wrong data, and the new test only asserts `queued is not None`, so the regression ships undetected.

[BUG] `to_dict()` uses `asdict()`, which leaves `queued` as a raw `datetime` object inside the dict that is passed as a Celery task kwarg (`assignment_source_dict`) in sync.py, and most Celery serializers (JSON) cannot encode datetime. `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs={... "assignment_source_dict": assignment_source.to_dict() ...})` fails to serialize when an assignment_source is present (i.e., on every inbound integration-triggered reassignment), raising a serialization EncodeError and silently dropping the outbound sync — and `from_dict` has no string→datetime parsing to reconstruct `queued` on the worker side either.

[ADVISORY] `sync_status_outbound` gained an `assignment_source` parameter but no call site in the diff passes it and the cycle guard in `should_sync` is only exercised on the assignee path, leaving the sibling status-sync path ungated — the same infinite ping-pong the diff claims to prevent still exists for status changes. A status resolution loop between two linked integrations (or the same integration) continues uninterrupted; a user who reads the PR title 'cross-system issue synchronization' will assume cycle protection covers status too, and no test in the diff verifies status-cycle behavior.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds a matching-source (cycle-suppressed) test and a default (assignment_source=None) test, but no test covers the headline propagation behavior: an assignment sourced from integration A being synced outward to linked issues of a different integration B. The comment in should_sync ('This should still allow other integrations to propagate changes outward') is the core requirement of the feature and is completely unverified; a regression that drops assignment_source=None-guard logic and blocks all cross-system propagation would pass the entire new test suite.

[ADVISORY] The AssignmentSource test suite never exercises a full to_dict→from_dict round trip through the task boundary, and `from_dict` does not validate types, so a dict with `queued` as an ISO string (the shape a JSON-serialized task payload would produce) reconstructs an AssignmentSource whose `queued` field is a str. The serialization contract between sync.py's `to_dict()` producer and the worker-side `from_dict()` consumer is hand-maintained on both ends with zero shared test; when the datetime serialization issue surfaces, the drift produces a silently mistyped `queued` field rather than the None fallback the error handling promises.

[BUG] The `queued` field default `timezone.now()` is evaluated once at class-definition (module import) time, so every AssignmentSource instance shares the process-start timestamp instead of the enqueue time. Any cycle-detection or freshness logic relying on `queued` gets a stale, identical timestamp for the entire worker process lifetime; the field's stated meaning (when the sync was queued) is never actually recorded.

[BUG] sync_group_assignee_outbound puts `assignment_source.to_dict()` — containing a raw `datetime` under the `queued` key — into celery `apply_async` kwargs, which the default JSON task serializer cannot encode. Once sync_group_assignee_inbound (which always sets assignment_source) runs, every queued sync_assignee_outbound task fails at publish time with a JSON EncodeError, so inbound-driven assignee sync silently stops propagating to all other linked integrations.

[BUG] from_dict does not convert the `queued` value back to a datetime, so a round-tripped AssignmentSource holds a `str` in a field typed `datetime` (and a dict missing `queued` silently falls back to the frozen import-time default). Any consumer that does datetime arithmetic or comparisons on `source.queued` on the worker side gets a TypeError or nonsensical ordering; the type annotation makes this failure invisible to static checks.

[ADVISORY] Rolling-deploy skew: new code enqueues sync_assignee_outbound with a fourth kwarg `assignment_source_dict`, but pre-deploy workers define `sync_assignee_outbound(external_issue_id, user_id, assign)` and will raise TypeError on the unexpected kwarg. During a deploy window, any inbound assignee sync that enqueues with a non-None assignment_source_dict hits old workers and the task errors out (with retries), dropping assignee propagation that worked before the deploy.

[ADVISORY] The abstract `sync_status_outbound` signature gains an `assignment_source` parameter, but no code path in this diff passes it to status sync — the assignee task calls `sync_assignee_outbound`, whose abstract signature is left unchanged — making the status-side parameter dead scope not traceable to any requirement in the PR. Every concrete integration subclass now sees a new abstract kwarg that nothing populates; the next reader assumes status sync also carries the source and builds cycle logic on a parameter that is always None.

[ADVISORY] Under-scoping of the stated cycle-prevention invariant: the `sync_source` guard is wired only into the assignee outbound path (`should_sync("outbound_assignee", ...)`), while the status sync path (sync_status_inbound_task / should_sync("sync_status_outbound")) still propagates with no source, so the same integration that originated a status change will be echoed a status sync back, reproducing exactly the loop this PR claims to prevent. Inbound status webhooks from integration A trigger Group resolution/registry updates that sync status back out to A's linked issue, re-notifying A and looping; users on multi-integration orgs get the ping-pong the PR intends to eliminate, but only for assignee is it fixed.

[ADVISORY] A region-silo model module now imports from `sentry.integrations.services.assignment_source`, adding a model-layer dependency on the integrations service layer (the existing pattern keeps integrations imports inside method bodies, e.g. the deferred `from sentry.integrations.utils import sync_group_assignee_outbound` three lines below). Import-order/circular-import failures surface at module load time in silo test bootstraps and any future refactor of integrations.services, and the inconsistency (module-level vs function-level import of the same package in the same function) makes the next change here riskier than it looks.

[ADVISORY] The test method `test_from_dict_inalid_data` (typo for 'invalid') plus the suite's tests only cover dict round-trips; there is no test that a celery-kwargs round-trip of a real AssignmentSource survives serialization, and no test asserting the cycle guard via the task path for the deassign branch (only assign is covered). The datetime-serialization failure in to_dict and the deassign cycle-guard path both ship untested; a regression in either is caught only in production when inbound unassign stops propagating.

[BUG] The `queued` default is `timezone.now()` evaluated once at module import, so every AssignmentSource shares the import-time timestamp, and the raw datetime in `to_dict()` cannot be serialized by Celery's default JSON encoder, causing `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async` to raise EncodeError. In `sync_group_assignee_outbound` (utils/sync.py), `assignment_source.to_dict()` embeds a `datetime` in the task kwargs; `apply_async` with the default json serializer throws EncodeError, so any inbound-triggered assign (e.g. a Jira issue assignee change propagating to Sentry) never enqueues the outbound task and cross-system sync silently dies; additionally the frozen default means `queued` records process start time, not queue time.

[BUG] The base-class `should_sync` signature gained a `sync_source` parameter, but existing `IssueBasicIntegration` subclasses across the codebase that override `should_sync(self, attribute)` with the old signature raise TypeError when callers pass the new positional argument. Any provider integration (e.g. GitHub, GitLab, Jira-style providers) whose subclass overrides `should_sync(attribute)` without the new parameter crashes with `TypeError: should_sync() takes 2 positional arguments but 3 were given` the first time `sync_assignee_outbound` runs with an assignment_source, breaking issue sync for that provider entirely; the diff shows no sweep of implementers.

[BUG] The cycle-prevention guard was added only to the assignee path while `sync_status_outbound` gained an `assignment_source` parameter that no caller in the diff ever passes, leaving status sync loops unguarded and the new parameter dead. Status changes originating from an external integration still round-trip back to the same integration (status ping-pong cycles persist), so the PR's stated goal of preventing sync-cycles is only partially realized; the `assignment_source` kwarg on `sync_status_outbound` is an unexercised public surface that will drift from the real call sites.

[ADVISORY] `from_dict` returns None on malformed input, silently discarding the source attribution instead of surfacing a parse failure, and accepts wrong-typed values (e.g. `integration_id` as a string, `queued` as any object) without validation. A legacy-queued task or a payload drift that fails to parse yields `assignment_source=None`, which converts a same-integration change into an unguarded outbound sync — the cycle-prevention control silently degrades to off, restarting the ping-pong loop the design exists to prevent.

[BUG] sync_assignee_outbound now unconditionally passes assignment_source= to installation.sync_assignee_outbound, but no concrete integration implementation of sync_assignee_outbound is updated in this diff to accept the keyword. For every provider subclass (Jira, GitHub, GitLab, etc.) whose sync_assignee_outbound signature does not include assignment_source, an outbound assignee sync raises TypeError: unexpected keyword argument 'assignment_source', breaking all outbound assignee syncing for those providers.

[BUG] The dataclass field default `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once at module import, so every AssignmentSource created without an explicit queued value carries the import-time timestamp, not the enqueue time. The 'queued' timestamp on every source produced via from_integration is stale (server-process start time), so any future staleness/dedup logic keyed on 'queued' operates on wrong data; to_dict also embeds this stale time into every task payload.

[BUG] assignment_source.to_dict() uses asdict(), which leaves the 'queued' field as a raw datetime object placed into Celery task kwargs via apply_async. Under a JSON-serializing Celery kombu transport, apply_async raises 'Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable' and the outbound assignee sync task never enqueues, breaking assignee sync for all issue-sync users on that broker; under pickle it round-trips, and from_dict then reconstructs with a datetime (fine) but any JSON path (e.g. replication/Redis inspection) fails.

[ADVISORY] from_dict returns None on any parse failure (missing/extra keys, wrong types), and sync_assignee_outbound then proceeds with parsed_assignment_source=None, silently disabling the same-integration cycle guard. A malformed or schema-drifted payload (e.g. a worker from a future deploy adding a field, or manual task inspection/edit) silently re-enables the assignee sync loop this PR exists to prevent — the guard fails open instead of failing closed, and operators get bouncing assignments with no error surfaced.

[ADVISORY] sync_status_outbound's abstract signature gains an assignment_source parameter, but nothing in this diff ever passes a status assignment_source, and no provider implementation in the diff accepts it — the parameter is inert. Provider subclasses that don't declare the kwarg (all of them, since none are updated here) are now signature-mismatched against the ABC contract, and the dead parameter suggests a future intent (status cycle-prevention) that has no producer, so the next implementer must guess whether to honor it.

[ADVISORY] In sync_group_assignee_inbound, when the inbound email matches no verified user the group is left unassigned but the deassign branch's outbound propagation of the source only covers the explicit unassign case — an inbound assign for an unmatched user never records or propagates the assignment_source, so a subsequent manual re-assign has no source context to suppress the echo. Users on organizations with multiple linked integrations will see partial cycle-prevention: assignments whose inbound payload fails user-matching fall back to unsourced outbound propagation on the next change, resurrecting the cross-integration bounce loop the PR intends to kill.

[BUG] sync_group_assignee_outbound passes assignment_source.to_dict() containing a raw datetime (`queued`) as a Celery task kwarg, which the default JSON task serializer cannot encode. Whenever an inbound integration assignment triggers the outbound sync path, sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async raises EncodeError (kombu Unable to serialize datetime), so the outbound assignee sync task never executes — the feature's core cross-system propagation silently dies for exactly the case it was built for (inbound-driven changes).

[ADVISORY] AssignmentSource.from_dict reconstructs the object via cls(**input_dict) with no field-type or key validation, and returns None on any mismatch, silently discarding the assignment source. Any malformed or drifted payload crossing the task-queue boundary (e.g., `queued` arriving as an ISO string after a serializer round-trip, or an unexpected extra key) makes from_dict return None, which disables the sync-cycle prevention in should_sync — two linked integrations then re-propagate assignments to each other in an infinite loop, hammering the external providers' APIs.

[ADVISORY] The `queued` default is `timezone.now()` evaluated once at class-definition time, so every AssignmentSource created without an explicit timestamp shares the process-import time. Operators comparing `queued` to infer when an assignment was initiated (e.g., for stale-loop or replay debugging) get a timestamp frozen at worker boot; the field also contributes the unserializable datetime that breaks the task enqueue.

[ADVISORY] The new cycle-prevention test has no positive control: it only asserts assert_not_called for a matching integration, and no test in the diff asserts that outbound assignee sync still happens when assignment_source belongs to a different integration. A regression that makes should_sync return False for any non-None sync_source (killing all cross-integration propagation — the exact scenario the code comment says should still be allowed) passes the entire suite, because the only test with a non-None assignment_source expects no call.

[BUG] AssignmentSource.queued defaults to timezone.now() evaluated once at import time and is a raw datetime, which AssignmentSource.to_dict() places into Celery apply_async kwargs via sync_group_assignee_outbound, where the default JSON serializer cannot serialize datetime — and no test round-trips to_dict() through apply_async or from_dict. The first real inbound-driven assignment enqueues sync_assignee_outbound with a datetime in assignment_source_dict, Celery's JSON encoder raises EncodeError, and the outbound sync task never runs; additionally from_dict on a JSON-decoded dict silently stores a string in queued with no validation, which the new tests (which only assert result is not None / queued is not None in-process) never detect.

[ADVISORY] The new dict-parsing and gating logic in the task body (AssignmentSource.from_dict on a malformed/partial dict returning None, then should_sync proceeding and sync_assignee_outbound receiving assignment_source=None) has zero test coverage — the only tests touching this path mock ExampleIntegration.sync_assignee_outbound and pass assignment_source=None from GroupAssignee.objects.assign. If from_dict swallows a valid-but-partial payload as None (its except clause silently converts any malformed Celery payload into a cycle-prevention bypass), no test fails; a developer changing from_dict's error handling or the None-fallback behavior in the task gets green tests while production inbound-triggered syncs silently lose their cycle-prevention guard.

[BUG] The `queued` field's default is `timezone.now()` evaluated once at class-definition time, so every AssignmentSource constructed without an explicit `queued` shares a single stale timestamp fixed at module import. Field-fidelity loss: the `queued` timestamp recorded for inbound-echo detection/cycle debugging is wrong for every payload after process start, and any consumer comparing queued times or relying on it for staleness sees import-time values; on long-running workers this is hours or days off.

[BUG] `to_dict()` returns a dict containing a raw `datetime` (`queued` field) which is sent as a Celery task kwarg in `sync_group_assignee_outbound.apply_async`, a payload crossing a process/queue boundary with a type the JSON transport cannot serialize. With the default JSON task serializer, `apply_async(kwargs={... "assignment_source_dict": ... datetime ...})` raises a serialization/encode error and the outbound assignee-sync task is never enqueued, so assignee changes silently stop propagating to linked external issues for every sync that carries a source (i.e., every inbound-driven assignment).

[BUG] The task now calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(external_issue, user, assign=assign, assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source)`, but this diff updates only the abstract signature on `IssueSyncIntegration.sync_assignee_outbound` — no concrete provider implementation (Jira, GitHub, GitLab, VSTS, etc.) is updated in this diff to accept the new `assignment_source` keyword. Every existing provider implementation whose signature does not include `assignment_source` (and does not swallow it via `**kwargs`) raises `TypeError: sync_assignee_outbound() got an unexpected keyword argument 'assignment_source'`, failing the outbound assignee sync task — and third-party/out-of-tree integrations are broken by the same silent public-surface change with no deprecation path.

[ADVISORY] `from_dict` swallows malformed payloads and returns None with no logging, silently disabling the cycle-pretection the whole feature exists to provide. If a queued payload is truncated/corrupted (or an older-format dict without `queued` fails to reconstruct), the task proceeds with `parsed_assignment_source = None`, `should_sync` skips the same-integration check, and the assignee change echoes back to the originating integration — reintroducing the sync cycle with zero signal to operators debugging it.

[ADVISORY] The new behavior-bearing logic in this diff (allow cross-integration propagation when the source integration differs from the target) has no test — only the matching-source suppression case is covered, so the feature's actual purpose (cross-system sync) is unverified. A regression in `should_sync` that blocks all outbound sync (e.g., an over-broad check or a None-handling slip in `org_integration`) passes this suite, and cross-integration assignee propagation silently stops for all customers; the uncovered behavior is the primary product behavior of the PR.

[BUG] sync_group_assignee_outbound passes assignment_source.to_dict() — which contains a raw datetime under the 'queued' key (asdict does not stringify datetimes) — as a celery apply_async kwarg, which the JSON task serializer cannot encode. Any assign/deassign with a non-None assignment_source (i.e. every inbound-triggered assignment) raises kombu's EncodeError/TypeError at enqueue time, the outbound sync task is never dispatched, and the external issue assignee silently desyncs from Sentry while the inbound operation reports success.

[BUG] The dataclass default `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once at module import time, so every AssignmentSource instance ever created shares the same frozen import-time timestamp. The 'queued' timestamp is meaningless for ordering/debugging — every queued assignment across all deployments of the process reports the moment the module was imported; anyone using it to diagnose stale-queue or cycle issues is misdirected. The fix is field(default_factory=timezone.now).

[ADVISORY] from_dict returns None on any parse failure, and sync_assignee_outbound (sync_assignee_outbound.py lines 50-54) then calls should_sync with sync_source=None, which re-enables the outbound sync the cycle-guard was meant to block. A malformed or partially-serialized assignment_source_dict (e.g. a dict whose 'queued' value fails datetime coercion semantics, or extra keys from a future schema) silently disables cycle prevention: the task runs, calls sync_assignee_outbound to the same integration that originated the change, and re-triggers the ping-pong the feature exists to stop — with no log or error surfaced anywhere.

[ADVISORY] The cycle guard only suppresses the outbound assignee sync when should_sync is consulted with a sync_source; the inbound path in sync_group_assignee_inbound constructs AssignmentSource from the integration, but any inbound assignee change arriving through a path that does not thread assignment_source (e.g. webhooks calling GroupAssignee.objects.assign without the new kwarg) will re-emit an outbound sync and can still start a cross-integration loop. Two integrations (A and B) both linked to the same group still form an A→Sentry→B→Sentry→A cycle because each integration's guard only matches its own integration_id; the 'this should still allow other integrations to propagate changes outward' comment describes the intended design but the diff provides no loop-termination (no hop count / queued-timestamp cutoff), so the persisted-but-unused 'queued' field suggests termination was intended and is missing.

[ADVISORY] to_dict returns the raw datetime under 'queued' but from_dict never converts it back, so a round-tripped AssignmentSource carries a value whose type differs depending on whether the instance came from from_integration (datetime) or from_dict (whatever the transport delivered, e.g. a string), and the dataclass does no validation. Any consumer comparing or sorting on 'queued' (the field exists solely to record when the change was queued) gets type-inconsistent values depending on the path; combined with the default_factory issue above, the field cannot be relied on for any ordering or staleness decision.
